utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes. The case number is IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I shall now ask for the appearances, please. The Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Counsel. For the Prosecution, David Re, Ekkehard Withopf, and Kimberly Fleming, as the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good afternoon. I'm Edina Residovic, Defence counsel for General Hadzihasanovic, and members of the team are Mr. Stephane Bourgon and Mirna Milanovic, a member of the Defence team. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Defence of Mr. Kubura, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, Mr. Rodney Dixon, and our assistant Mr. Mulalic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to welcome the Prosecution, the Defence, and the accused. If I understood you correctly, I think the Defence team would like to take the floor before we bring the witness in. I shall therefore give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence wanted to raise three issues with you this afternoon. The first has to do with the request made by the Prosecution filed yesterday with regard to protective measures. We should like to inform the Trial Chamber that the motion was filed by the Prosecutor yesterday at 12.15 and the Defence was not in a position, therefore, to receive the motion before it was discussed during the court session. We, however, know that probably in the course of this trial we will have several instances where the parties will not be able to send in their documents to the opposite side on time, but we should like to make the Trial Chamber aware of this and to ask both parties whenever possible - and I think that this is possible in the majority of cases - to disclose the request to the Defence, or if we are tabling the motion that we send our motions in to the Prosecution, giving them and us enough time to be able to have the opposite party prepare so as to be able to present the relevant argumentation before the Trial Chamber, with respect to the motion in question. At the beginning of this trial, Mr. President - and that is why we should like to raise certain procedural issues of this nature, which we consider are of interest to the parties, precisely because we are starting the trial; we're at the beginning of the trial, the initial stages - the second question, which the Defence wish to raise, is quite simply a piece of information which we'd like to give to the Trial Chamber. And we undertook this as an obligation on our part on Friday, and we tabled a request to the Trial Chamber today with our proposals to facilitate the Trial Chamber in resolving the question of the impossibility the Defence has had in its access to documents and archives of the European Monitors, observers. As the Defence considers for its part that it should contribute to a speedy and efficacious trial, although the Defence is fully aware that this is exclusively the right of the Trial Chamber, in its motion and request it also put forward a proposal according to which, according to Rule 26 bis it reviewed whether a response to this motion requires 14 days or whether the Trial Chamber will modify that deadline. Mr. President, yesterday we received a new list from the Prosecution for the new exhibits and witnesses. We now ask permission for those same reasons to speed up a ruling on this issue, for the Trial Chamber to allow us today to state our views on that list; or, if the Trial Chamber considers it to be more appropriate, to ask us to do so in written form perhaps. The list -- the newly compiled list from the Prosecutor is one we received yesterday. Having considered it, we seem to feel that the list contains certain exhibits which have not as yet been disclosed to the Defence teams, and other exhibits which probably have been disclosed but were not on the previous lists supplied to us by the Prosecution. Second, we consider it to be very important that the Prosecutor, after almost two and a half years since the accused first appeared before this Tribunal and after the pre-trial motion, should ensure a final and complete list of exhibits, a comprehensive list, which they wish to use in the course of this trial because we consider this to be indispensable for the trial to evolve in just fashion. It is very important for the Defence to have all the exhibits and evidence disclosed to it so that it could take the necessary steps needed for it to investigate the authenticity of the documents or to prepare itself for making proposals or objections to these exhibits being tendered into evidence. Now, may I turn to the list of witnesses disclosed to us by the Prosecution. The Defence would like to point out that some of the witnesses that have been added to this list, the additional witnesses, will be called to testify, as far as we can see, from the witness statements about the same facts and circumstantial evidence that some other witnesses will be testifying to, witnesses who are already on the Prosecutor's list. These additional witnesses will be testifying to the same facts. Of course, it is up to the Prosecution to decide how many and which witnesses to call and it is also up to the Trial Chamber to agree in having these witnesses called or to perhaps decide which should be called. We consider that, in view of our position, it would be a good idea if we pointed out that some of these witnesses were testifying to the same facts, just like the testimony of the witnesses on the list that already existed. Now, we don't object to this and this time we have ten or eleven new witnesses. We don't mind. We consider that the Prosecution has pursuant to Rule 65 ter and the Status Conference, he let us know and he said he would have an additional six to eight witnesses on that occasion. However, we should like to point out that after the presentation of evidence has got underway we can see now that the presentation of evidence and the exhibits are not following the planned time limit and schedule, so we would like to draw your attention to that. We should like to draw attention of the Trial Chamber to that fact. And the final proposal by the Defence, with respect to the motion filed by the Prosecutor, is that we should like to prevail upon the Trial Chamber to ask the Prosecution to send us a complete, comprehensive, and final list and that any additional requirements and requests should be put forward only under extraordinary circumstances, which should be expounded upon by the Prosecution. So that, briefly, Mr. President, are the proposals and -- that we have to make, and we should like to ask the Trial Chamber to make a ruling on them. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Defence counsel of Mr. Kubura like to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a joint proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before giving the floor to the Prosecution at this stage of the proceeding, we will address the three items but in the reverse order. The last point related to the list of witnesses as well as the list of exhibits, the new list of exhibits. The Defence counsel has just told us as regards the list of exhibits, there were some exhibits missing Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that had been mentioned on this new list, and it seems like the Defence team does not have these exhibits. So I would like the Prosecution to contact the Defence team with a view to disclosing those missing exhibits as quickly as possible. I assume this will not raise any technical problem. As far as a list of witnesses and exhibits are concerned, if the Defence team accepts the fact or does not, they should send something in writing, because this witness list was provided in writing and the Defence team should also provide in writing something to the fact that some of the witnesses on the previous list and the new list are identical; therefore, there's no point in calling witnesses to say the same thing, because in certain cases these are the same witnesses. As far as the exhibits are concerned, if the Defence has any objections or any issue to raise, then the Defence team should inform us in writing. We will be calling these witnesses at the beginning of next year. If you set a time limit which, let's assume, could be the 12th of January, that would give you enough time to look into this at leisure and you could then send us something in writing by the 12th of January. As you know, the 12th of January marks the end of the winter recess. In addition, you have also noted, I'm sure, that the Trial Chamber was seized by the Prosecution and the report of the General Reinhardt was filed. You therefore also have the possibility to challenge the content of this report in due time, and you have up until the 12th of January to do so. As far as the second point is concerned - namely, the request you've filed pertaining to those exhibits relating to the European Union - you were worried ahead of time by the fact that the Prosecution might state its position two weeks beforehand. From what I understand with my exchange with the Prosecution, I think they do not oppose any objection on principle to your requests. So could the Prosecution let us know as quickly as possible that this is not a problem so that we can draft this decision and render it. So I think we should find a solution to this point fairly quickly. I shall now address the first point, which related to the fact that you were surprised by the fact that you were not informed about those protective measures to be granted to the witness we will be hearing today. Admittedly, on reading Article 69 -- Rule 69 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, it is mentioned that protective measures, when they are requested by the Prosecution, are measures which should be requested by the Prosecution. It is not stipulated that the Prosecution has to inform the Defence team about this. But if we turn to Article 75 and we combine the two articles, 75 and the previous, 69, we understand that the Trial Chamber on request of one of the two parties order the appropriate measures if, and in the event that these measures do not -- or that these measures are consistent with the rights of the accused. We will therefore assume that the Prosecution must avail itself of its position. So it's a combination of the two Rules which apply here, and the Defence team and the Prosecution need to discuss this. Maybe the Defence team, one day you will ask to have protective measures; in that case, the Prosecution needs to be able to state its position also. So it would be desirable if in the future the Prosecution, every time it wishes to request protective measures, that they let the Defence team know in due time so that in the event that the fundamental rights of the accused may be effected, that the Defence team can stipulate this in writing, because the request of the Prosecution is made in writing; the Defence has to, therefore, be made in writing also. If there are exceptional circumstances - which is the case, because we have a very -- we are very limited by time - you could then discuss this verbally and we shall render our decision. But it is, of course, desirable that you get the information well ahead of time. And I think this has to be discussed by both parties. And this is against the backdrop of this exchange that this trial will go ahead in the best conditions possible. I hope this will be the case in the future also, and I understand that both parties should by so doing reveal the truth as best as possible. As regards this particular point, does the Prosecution wish to take the floor? We will then pursue the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Very, very briefly. Thank you, Your Honours. Of course, we note everything that Your Honour has just said. The Prosecution will, of course, endeavour to avoid repetition in any evidence that it calls. The Prosecution informed the Trial Chamber and Defence, in relation to those additional seven witness we propose tendering, we don't propose tendering them immediately in January, by any stretch of the imagination. That would certainly be called midway through the trial, maybe February, March. So the Defence should be assured that they will have sufficient time to prepare in respect of that. The -- just one other matter. That's in relation to the confidential motion we filed on Friday, the 8th of December -- sorry, Monday, Monday, the 8th -- the Prosecution's motion to amend its list of witnesses and exhibits. As we've noted, and the only reason we filed it confidentially was because there was some information in the body of the motion relating to some information about the witnesses. We appended General Reinhardt's report to that motion filed confidentially. We actually should have written "partially confidential" on the -- on the cover. I would ask Your Honours to lift the confidentiality in relation to General Reinhardt's report so that's publicly available. There's no reason why it should be filed confidentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask Mr. Registrar, who's reading the transcript, to bring in the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It's the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, can you hear what I am saying? Can you hear the translation? Can you hear me? Fine. Please sit down. Before I give the floor to the Prosecution that will be questioning the witness, I would like to ask the registrar whether those protective measures, i.e. distortion of the face and voice, are still valid, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the protective measures are in place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Before hearing the witness, in order to gain time, pursuant to Article 90(F)(i) feels that it is our duty to remind the witness and the parties of a number of Rules contained in the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. I should like to turn now to the witness and tell him the following: You are a Prosecution witness. Your testimony is made under oath. You have the duty, therefore, to tell the truth. If the Trial Chamber feels that you have deliberately and voluntarily made a false testimony, the Trial Chamber is entitled to launch a proceeding against you. In the event that you would be proven guilty of a false testimony, you would be liable for a fine of 100.000 Euros and a seven-year prison term. I would also let you know that if you refuse to answer any one or other question, despite the question put to you by the Chamber, you could be liable for a contempt proceeding; in the event, the sentencing range is exactly the same as for a false testimony. I should like to remind you that before this Tribunal you are a simple witness. You are not accused. You are entitled to refuse to say anything which might go against your interests. And in that case, the Trial Chamber can ask you to nevertheless answer this question, even though you may feel it may incriminate you. In that case, the testimony you would be making cannot be used as a piece of evidence against you before this Tribunal, either in -- before this Tribunal, any other national jurisdiction, or in Bosnia. I am just saying this so that you can testify freely before the Judges of this Tribunal and, given the fact that protective measures have been granted, nobody knows who you are, nobody outside this courtroom can actually see your face, and nobody can hear your voice. Nobody can recognise your voice. This is what I wanted to tell the witness. As far as the parties are concerned, the Prosecution and the Defence, the Trial Chamber would like to remind both parties that they are in control of the examination-in-chief and cross-examination of the witness so as to render the examination and the presentation of exhibits in an efficient manner in order to reveal the truth. We are now talking about Rule 99. In addition, the Trial Chamber is in charge of the examinations before this Court, with a view to avoiding any form of harassment or intimidation whatsoever, pursuant to Article 75(D). The Trial Chamber felt it was important to remind the parties of the conditions in which this trial shall unfold. I hope this will be the case in the future. The witness is now informed about the fact that he can freely testify. I shall therefore give the floor to the Prosecution. I think the Prosecution still needs to ask the witness a number of questions. Let me remind you that it is now twenty to 3.00. We shall have a break in an hour's time, around quarter to 4.00. We shall have a 20/25-minute break at quarter to 4.00 and resume after the break. Given the time needed by the Prosecution and the time needed by the Defence for its cross-examination, I believe this witness will be with us until 7.00 p.m., unless we finish earlier, but this witness will certainly be with us all afternoon and the other witness on the list will probably be called tomorrow. This will depend, of course, how things unfold. In order not to lose any more time, I shall now give the floor to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness BA [Resumed]. When we broke yesterday you had a copy of the exhibit marked for identification, Exhibit P12.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could that please be returned to the ELMO for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday you marked the line of your advancement from the confluence of the Bosna and Lasva Rivers to Dusina, to the Muslim part of town, where you stayed overnight. Yesterday I was asking you about soldiers from your own company and others. I want to ask you whether you know of a group called the Blue Falcons.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Blue Falcons?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said, the Blue Falcons, as in birds like hawks, or eagles. Witness BA, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Did you hear my question? Did you know of a group called the Blue Falcons, falcons like birds like hawks or eagles, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were a sabotage reconnaissance unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they part of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were they present in Dusina on either the 25th or 26th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you first see them in Dusina on the 25th or 26th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you told me that they were a sabotage reconnaissance unit. Where were the members of the Blue Falcons from? What I mean is -- by that I mean from where did the Blue Falcons recruit their members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You are aware that throughout the armies in the former Yugoslavia -- sorry, in Bosnia that various brigades and units recruited members from different specific areas. I'm asking you where the Blue -- which area the Blue Falcons recruited its members from; village, town, municipality, or wherever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In January 1993, when you were in Dusina, who was commanding the Blue Falcons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serif Patkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was Serif Patkovic's position in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade when you were in Dusina in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just get you to clarify the answer to the question, which was "I don't know exactly." You used the word "exactly." What was your knowledge of the position of Serif Patkovic within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion was not complete, a full complement of it. There were one or two companies. It wasn't a complete battalion. So I don't know what position he occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A moment ago you said you couldn't remember exactly where you first saw the Blue Falcons in Dusina. Where did you see them in Dusina, if you can't remember exactly where you first saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to give you incorrect information. If I say something, I would like to say exactly what I know, what I saw, and heard. Now, if that's not the case, then I would rather not answer the question in an inexact way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you couldn't remember exactly where you first saw them. I've moved on from there. I'm now asking you where you saw them in Dusina, as opposed to when you first saw them. So can you just direct your mind to seeing them in Dusina, as you said you did, and where it was that you saw them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A day before the conflict broke out, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And where was that that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them at the confluence in Lasva and Dusina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when you were in Dusina on the next day - that's the 26th of January - were the Blue Falcons there as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which part of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were divided in two groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. We'll take them -- we'll take them one at a time. Where was the group -- where did the group of the Blue Falcons that wasn't in Dusina, where did they go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, two captured members of those same Blue Falcons were supposed to be liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you expand on that? What do you mean? Where were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Lasva settlement controlled by the Croatian Defence Council and those two members just happened to be in the area before the conflict actually broke out, and so those two soldiers were captured by the Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you saying that one part of the -- one section of the Blue Falcons went there to liberate them and another section went somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the plan, to liberate them, nor was it an attack plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Two of the Blue Falcons required liberating from the HVO. You're saying some of the Blue Falcons went to liberate them. Did your group -- did you or members of your group go with them to liberate the captured Blue Falcon fighters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody went to free them. Quite simply they were deployed within the Muslim part of Lasva and at the confluence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I'll take you back to being in Dusina and the -- on the 26th of January and the Blue Falcons being divided into two groups. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber what the two groups were and how they were -- how they were divided, that is, where each of the two groups went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4/8:47 The first night nobody was sent anywhere. All the members of the Muslim unit were within the village. The only task was that if a conflict should break out -- because the HDZ had already captured two members of the 7th Muslim -- if a conflict were to break out, they were to protect the Muslim population in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm trying to ask you about, Witness BA, is what you said a few moments ago, about the Blue Falcons being divided into two groups on the 26th of January. So can you please concentrate on that part and tell the Trial Chamber on the 26th of January how were they divided and where did the two groups go.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know they were divided into two groups? You said a moment ago that you saw Blue Falcons there on the 26th of January.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because at Dusina I just saw some six or seven members of the Blue Falcons, which means they weren't all there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly be asked to speak up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, would you be able to speak a little bit more loudly in your answers so the interpreters can hear you a bit more clearly. Would you be able to do that? Thank you. Before we broke last night, we got to what happened in Dusina on the morning of the 26th of January, 1993. Now, you've mentioned some Blue Falcons there and you've mentioned your own group being there. Where did your group go on the morning of the 26th of January, 1993? When I say "your group," I mean your company, that is, the Musical Company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what the local population said, we received information that the headquarters of the HDZ was at Brdo, and that's the direction we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that where you've marked on the map? Would you please just look to the map to your right on the overhead projector there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you please mark with the same texter and please draw a line with the same arrow to the next place you went in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At about what time did you get to Dusina on the morning of the 26th of January -- sorry, Brdo, on the morning of the 26th of January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How early in the morning? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it light when you got there? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was already daylight.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did members of your Musical Company go to Brdo in the early -- after daylight on the 26th of January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The intention was to negotiate, to have them release the two captives.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That is, negotiate with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that to negotiate with the HVO commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did the negotiations occur?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the house, where Zvonko Rajic was put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who was Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the HVO that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who negotiated on behalf of the ABiH soldiers who negotiated with Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Elvedin Camdzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened when Elvedin Camdzic went to negotiate with Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They killed him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who killed who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The members of the HVO, the commander of our company.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Could you describe what happened so that the rest of us can imagine or have a picture of where you were and what you saw and how the person was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the Musical Company went to negotiate with the HVO; that means that the whole company didn't go, just part of it. Part of the company remained behind in the Muslim section of Dusina. Quite simply, they stayed behind, because they didn't want to shoot. When the negotiations started -- or rather, when members of the HVO were called to negotiate with our company commander, he went behind the house. He didn't intend to shoot. His rifle was lowered, beside his leg. But the members of the HVO started shooting nonetheless, and one bullet hit him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the reaction of your side -- what did your side do in response to your commander being shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the commander, we had two other wounded men, and then we opened fire in order to be able to pull out the two wounded men.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the civilians of the village of Dusina and Brdo when this exchange of fire was going on between the HVO and the 3rd Corps soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the two houses where, strictly speaking, there were no civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was Zvonko Rajic at the time of this exchange of fire when your commander was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the house from which the firing came.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did members of your company make contact with Zvonko Rajic in that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Can you describe to the Court how they did, how they managed to contact him, and what, if anything, was said to him, and what his response was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly how it happened. I don't remember which words were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to use the exact words, obviously, so long after the event, but doing your best of what you remember was the general effect of what was said, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to make a mistake in uttering any words myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have any impression now of the content of any communication, as opposed to the words used; that is, what they were talking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our company commander came out from behind a house. He went out into an open space, and he called out to Zvonko Rajic. And when he was called out to negotiate, the answer he got was a burst of gunfire as a response.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Following the burst of gunfire, what happened then? What was the next thing that happened after you tried to negotiate with Rajic and there was a burst of gunfire from their side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then there was an exchange of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many HVO members were firing at your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your answer said "five of six of us." I was asking you about how many HVO members were firing at your company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five or six.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they firing from the house where Zvonko Rajic was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the house they were in and from a position a little above the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Following this exchange of gunfire, did negotiations continue at any point between the HVO side and your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about an hour, an hour or two hours. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Rajic still in his house when the negotiations recommenced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How were the negotiations conducted? By that I mean did someone go into the house or was someone communicating with him from outside the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were in the house. We were outside, up by some other houses. So it was mostly outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were the respective numbers of the soldiers? You said there were five or six of them. How many of them -- how many of you, that is, ABiH soldiers, were in the vicinity of the house -- of the area where the HVO soldiers were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told us about negotiations with Rajic. Did you reach agreement with Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about two hours, after there was this exchange of gunfire for about two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was the agreement that your side reached with the -- with Rajic and his HVO members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The agreement that was reached was that both of us should take off our ammunition clips and move in the direction of Lasva to solve the problem with the captives.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was the agreement. Did you in fact remove your magazine clips?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Rajic and the HVO people come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to Rajic's and the HVO members' weapons when they came out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They carried them with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did your group and Rajic and the other HVO members go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the road towards Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What I want you to do now is to get the map again, which is to your right, get the black texter, and mark where the road to Lasva is -- mark the route you took from then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said, I think, there were -- are you able to tell us today the exact number of HVO soldiers that were accompanying you along the road towards Lasva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the five include Zvonko Rajic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again about civilians in the village after or about the time of the exchange of gunfire between your group and the HVO and the successful negotiations for the HVO members to come out. What can you tell the Trial Chamber about the presence of civilians in that area over those few hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the house Zvonko Rajic was in, the civilians were brought, the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd like you to expand upon that. You said the civilians -- the civilian Croats were brought. I want you to tell us how many Croat civilians and who brought them to the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how many civilians there were. I don't know how many soldiers there were who brought them there. They didn't bring them to the house but to near the house, where there was an exchange of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Which side were the soldiers from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not clear on what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said soldiers brought the Croat civilians to the house -- or near the house. Were the soldiers HVO soldiers or ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you don't know exactly. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber roughly how many soldiers there were and how many soldiers there were escorting roughly how many civilians. You don't need to be precise.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, we didn't hear your last answer. Could you just say it a bit more loudly so the interpreters can hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 1 and 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't quite understand that answer. Firstly can we divide it into two. Approximately, roughly, how many civilians were being escorted to the place near the house? Then I'll ask you about the soldiers. I mean, was it less than ten, more than ten, less than five, more than five, less than twenty, more than twenty? That's the sort of information we're interested in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think more than ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Now, what about the soldiers? Again, less than five, more than five, less than ten, more than ten, less than twenty, more than twenty, or whatever.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you about the soldiers. I don't know how many exactly there were. You couldn't see them. Perhaps you could see two of them. Now, any others that might have been there, you couldn't actually see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Well, the ones -- the soldiers you saw, were they members of your company or of the Blue Falcons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you know of not the names but who any of the civilians were in this group. I don't need the names, just if you know the identity, as in their relationship to someone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that Zvonko Rajic's wife was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Zvonko Rajic's wife was in this group of civilians who were being brought to a place near the house where he was; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was Zvonko Rajic made aware of the fact during negotiations that his wife was outside in the presence or company of armed ABiH soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that one of the negotiating points?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was the fact that Zvonko Rajic's wife was outside, in the presence of armed ABiH soldiers, one of the points that was used when your company negotiated with Zvonko Rajic to come out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sporadic shooting lasted about two hours, so Zvonko Rajic didn't want to negotiate until the civilians were brought in and until he realised that his wife was amongst them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did he come to find out that his wife was outside amongst the armed ABiH soldiers when he was inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because our members informed him that she was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that one of the factors that -- was that one of the things that led him to come out, from what you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first he didn't want to go out. Then the negotiations started, that both sides should take off their magazine clips from their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Witness BA, I'm not asking you that. I'm asking you about Zvonko Rajic's wife and the fact that your soldiers told him that his wife was -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that. My question is: How did you -- how did Zvonko Rajic become aware that his wife was outside in the presence of armed ABiH soldiers? How did he come to know that? Did he see it or did someone tell him or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was told. But I think he could also see it, because they were brought quite close up to the house, so he could see that for himself. That's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. You said he was told. What I just want you to tell the Trial Chamber is who told him and what did they say. Not using the precise or exact words but the effect of what was said to him inside the house.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the effect was that he undertook to negotiate immediately afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, what was said to him about his wife being outside in the presence of armed ABiH soldiers that led him to undertake to negotiate immediately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't start to negotiate straight away, as I said a moment ago. This went on -- the sporadic shooting went on for some time. And it was only after some 50 minutes had gone by that he started to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. If I can take you back to the map on which you drew your route with Zvonko Rajic and the four other HVO members, back towards the road to Lasva. You've just told us about some civilians -- some contact with civilians when Zvonko Rajic was in the house. Did you have -- did you meet anyone on the way? When I say "on the way," I mean on the road, the route you've just -- you've marked from Brdo to Lasva.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't. I don't remember, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you go straight to Lasva from Brdo or did you stop somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped. So we were going from Brdo towards Lasva and we stopped some 2 to 3 hundred metres before Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you stop, Witness BA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we received information that members of the HVO had set up a barricade or, rather, an ambush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you recall how you got that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the locals told us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you react to this information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We lost -- the members of the HVO who were with us -- actually, we didn't think that they were keeping to their part of the agreement with respect to the weapons in Lasva, so we took their weapons from them and a part started to return.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Return to Dusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, back to Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What did Zvonko Rajic do on the way back to Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took the road and after 1 or 2 hundred metres Zvonko Rajic attempted to escape.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did he do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He just separated from his group and started running.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which direction did he run?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Across a meadow, in the direction of Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the reaction of your group to Zvonko Rajic attempting to escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We shouted out to him to stop. He paid no attention. And we started shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say "we," how many of you fired at Zvonko Rajic -- I'm sorry. You said "shooting." In what direction did you shoot and how many of you shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you one of the shooters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In which direction did you shoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Zvonko Rajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he still running when you shot at him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hit him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was he shot? On which part of his body was he shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was shot in several places, all in his lower extremities, the bottom half of his body.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you mean his legs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below his hips and in his legs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did he fall to the ground as a result of being shot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were the four other HVO members when you shot Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were together with the rest of our members on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just told us that you shot Zvonko Rajic and he was lying on the ground wounded by shots to his lower extremities. What did your group do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear. I'm not following the last thing you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Zvonko Rajic was lying on the ground shot. What did you and the members of your company do then? Did you leave him there? Did you go to him? Did you do something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went up to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the four HVO members? Did they go with you to Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You called them over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ask them to do something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you ask the HVO members to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As he was wounded, we asked them to pick him up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They took him up and took him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About what time of the morning was this when you shot Zvonko Rajic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps around 9.00. 9.00; perhaps a little later. I can't quite remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Where did your soldiers and the HVO members who were carrying Zvonko Rajic go then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they took the road back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Back where? Was it back to Brdo or back to Lasva?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Back towards Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How far did you get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 200 metres. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you stop after about 200 metres or so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the unit withdrew, and the other part stayed in the lower half to provide security. We lost our -- we were no longer certain what we -- we weren't certain that the HVO wouldn't attack us, so part of the unit stayed in that lower area.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've told us about the presence of Blue Falcon members in Dusina on the 26th of January. Did you see any members of the Blue Falcons on your way back to Brdo with the injured Zvonko Rajic and the four HVO members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just have a moment to consult the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've already asked you --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I thank Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've already asked you about Serif Patkovic, who you said was the commander of the Blue Falcons. Did you see him in Dusina when you were with the injured Zvonko Rajic and the four HVO members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about in Brdo -- or sorry, on the road towards Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where you did you take the injured Zvonko Rajic to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed providing security along the road should there be a conflict, if there was shooting again. So I stayed on the road to provide security there, I and four other members.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were with Zvonko Rajic, who had been shot in the leg, and four injured HVO members, and you were walking back with them towards Brdo. You said you stopped. Why did you stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stopped straight after Zvonko Rajic had been wounded, when he started to flee. That's where we stopped, as Zvonko Rajic and four or five others took the road, and I, as I said, stayed on the road to secure the road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. -- sorry, Witness BA, you are aware of why you are giving evidence before this Trial Chamber, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You are aware that you're here to give evidence about the shooting of Zvonko Rajic and an incident involving Serif Patkovic, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence. Counsel, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecutor has just started to cross-examine the witness, so that we object. In an examination-in-chief, questions like that of the witness are improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not cross-examining the witness. I'm asking the witness if he knows why he's here in accordance with the summary that we filed. And Your Honours have a copy of the summary. The witness can answer yes or no; we can remind him of why he's here; we can move on. I just don't want to waste the Trial Chamber's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall address the witness directly, in the light of this difficulty. The witness is here to testify about what he has seen. Can the witness answer this question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The witness knows that he must tell the truth, because you made a solemn declaration whereby you were going to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And precisely because of that solemn declaration I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you are telling the truth, answer either by saying yes or no or answer the question exactly, please. We shall now adjourn and both parties will be able to have a rest during this break. And we shall resume the examination-in-chief at five minutes past 4.00. We shall have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now five past 4.00. We are resuming this hearing. We will have another break at half past 5.00, have a 20-minute break and resume around ten to 6.00 or five to 6.00 and finish at 7.00. Given this time frame, I don't know whether we can complete the cross-examination during that time. Can the Defence tell us how much time they will be needing -- the Prosecution, sorry -- how much time the Prosecution will be needing for the rest of its examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't. Your Honours can see how slowly it's going. I think Your Honours are aware of the scope of the evidence I'm trying to elicit and how long it's taking. We've gone way beyond our estimate now. I just can't give a realistic estimate at the moment. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, under these circumstances, if we haven't finished, the witness will have to come back tomorrow. So please proceed with your questions. The Defence, you would like to take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, very briefly. During the break, the Trial Chamber -- just before the break, the Trial Chamber had told the witness that the Prosecution could ask a question directly to the witness, and the witness would be asked to answer either by saying yes or no. We believe, Your Honour, that this procedure amounts to the fact that the Prosecution will be entitled to ask leading questions. The situation we are confronted with is the following: The Prosecution is asking questions and does not get the answers it wishes to get; the witness has been warned formally by the Trial Chamber and has been told exactly what he was to do. He answered that he was telling the truth and that he had understood that he had to tell the truth. Under these circumstances, Your Honour, we believe that, A, the Trial Chamber should maintain its decision taken last week - in other words, not allow the Prosecution to refresh the memory of the witness as regards his statement, and also not entitle the Prosecution to ask leading questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When we, the Trial Chamber, asked that the Prosecution ask questions and the witness answer either by saying yes or no, these questions were not to be leading questions, of course. That stands to reason. So I shall give the floor back now to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to show you a diagram, Witness BA. It's a diagram you prepared on which you've marked a number of events and a diagram which corresponds with the map on which you've drawn, which is P12 -- I'm sorry, was it -- I haven't tendered it, but P12 MFI. It should be on the screen in front of you now, Witness BA. Can you look down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just wait a minute, please. Before giving the floor to the Prosecution, yesterday we were referring to a document, P12, which had not officially been tendered into evidence. This is not the document we have just been given. It was in effect the map, which we have just seen on the ELMO. So this is yesterday's document. This document has got nothing to do with it. I answered and anticipated the question of the Defence. Am I right? So we are now talking about this exhibit, P12, which had not been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, we're not. We're talking about the diagram which is now being displayed on Sanction, which the witness has in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness BA, in front of you is a diagram which you prepared on which you have marked various locations which correspond with the map, which is P12 on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Where does this diagram come from? What is the source of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness. The witness drew a diagram, marking on it very places. I can hand a translation in English to Your Honours. It's location -- X1, location where commanding officer Camdzic was killed; 2, where bullet was fired; 3, where Rajic was fired; 4 -- and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as we understood it from the documents we received from the Prosecution, this diagram is a component part of the previous statement and cannot be used to refresh the witness's memory of what he said in his previous statement or testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution isn't attempting to do that. The Prosecution is attempting to facilitate proceedings by rather than have the witness draw in court the various things which he has described to date to show him a document he prepared on which he has written the various things and to use that as an aide-memoire for the proceedings and to tender it at the appropriate stage. I'm not attempting to refresh the witness's memory, and it's not a statement. It's a diagram he drew, which if Your Honour looks Your Honour can see from the -- Your Honours can see from the wavy lines, the road, it actually corresponds with P12, which hasn't been tendered yet. And I have another document which the witness marked out of court on which -- actually handing it up -- which he has actually drawn in yellow on the map, which is an identical copy of P12, to correspond to -- to correspond this with that. And I wish to use both as an aide-memoire to the witness in his evidence to facilitate presentation of evidence before the Trial Chamber and to ensure that the Trial Chamber has the most accurate and correct and truthful version of events before it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Trial Chamber has understood you correctly, this document entitled "Exhibit P22" is a document which the witness has drafted at the time he was being

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: ago. In other words, you want to use this document, which was part and parcel of his former statement, together with a map, which we saw yesterday and which he mentioned the events. So this does pose the question: Can we include this document marked P22, which is a document that goes back to his written statement, in relation to the document he authenticated recently? The Defence seems to challenge this, as it mentioned, because the witness can be asked during the examination-in-chief, to be asked to indicate the itinerary on the map. If he agrees, he does pinpoint the specific locations. Is that the point of view of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. If the Prosecution so wishes, the witness can show and draw in the road that he described and testified about before this Trial Chamber here today. If the Prosecution wishes to ask him to do so, he can do so straight away now. But the problem is that it is the component part of a statement -- of the previous statement. So it's not the diagram that's the problem, it's that there's a text underneath and that contains what the witness wishes to tell the witness [as interpreted], to remind him of his previous testimony and statement. And I don't think that is a proper way ask that it can be tendered and introduced into the trial proceedings in this way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As I've said, I'm not attempting to use it to refresh the witness's memory. I'm using it to facilitate the calling of evidence before the Trial Chamber. In the Prosecution's submission, I can -- I should be able to show him this document, which he drew on yesterday, in conjunction with one which he identified -- which he wrote on earlier. We'll get to the same point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Given the objection raised by the Defence, the Trial Chamber feels that the witness can be given a white sheet of paper. The witness will be asked to mention a number of things pertaining to your questions. We shall now take this document, P22, away. We shall give the witness a white sheet of paper. So you may ask him your questions very quickly and ask him to visualise or locate on this white sheet of paper those particular areas you are interested in. The Prosecution, you can do this rather quickly, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, you heard what His Honour said. What we want you to do is to draw on that piece of paper, draw a map marking the road to Lasva, Brdo, Dusina, the road to Visjnica, the junction of the Lasva and Bosna Rivers. Can you please draw those on as quickly as you possibly can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So it's taken us just under one minute. So please put this document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right, Witness BA. I want you to mark on it with the same pen the following thing, please: I want you to mark with an X1 where Elvedin Camdzic was killed, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Could you perhaps do a circle around that to make it a little bit clearer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Okay. X2, I want you to mark the spot where you shot Zvonko Rajic, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Can you mark -- I'm sorry, that was my fault. Can you please put "X2" in fairly large letters next to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you please mark the spot where Zvonko Rajic was killed, please, with "X3."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you please mark with "X4" the position where the people captured from Dusina were brought to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please now write and sign your name on the bottom of that piece of paper -- I'm sorry, don't, don't. My mistake. Would you please write "Witness BA" on the bottom of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] .

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour. Microphone for the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I was saying that as we are not in private session, if you would like the witness to authenticate his signature, you have to ask to have a -- to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It will suffice if he just -- for Prosecution's purposes if he just writes "Witness BA" on it, for the court record, and no one will know who he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that all right with you, the Defence team, "Witness BA"? So Witness, please, can you just write at the bottom of this sheet of paper "Witness BA," please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you please put the date on it as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. "Svedok BA" is written on here. I presume that in B/C/S "svedok" means "witness," does it? To make sure that this remains confidential, we shall -- Please, Madam Registrar, could you give me a confidential exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... P13, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's taken us all in all two minutes. This was a much better solution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- sorry, Witness, Witness BA for marking that diagram for us. On that diagram, you marked the position where Zvonko Rajic was killed. I want to tell the -- to describe, please, to the Trial Chamber how Zvonko Rajic was killed; that is, who killed him and how.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't describe that, because I was present.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, whether he was or was not present. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, your last answer was "I can't describe that because I was present." What I'm asking you to tell the Trial Chamber is to tell it, tell Their Honours, how Zvonko Rajic was killed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was not present. I didn't say "present." I said "not present."

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: When you said "present," where were you when Zvonko Rajic was killed, Witness BA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed at a place some 2 or 3 hundred metres lower down, and I marked it in the spot where I said "Zvonko Rajic, wounded."

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You've marked Zvonko Rajic -- the place where he was killed on the map. Presumably that means that you know that he was in fact killed, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After about an hour, I went up to the spot where Zvonko Rajic was, and according to what I saw myself you couldn't actually say whether he was dead, whether he'd already succumbed to his wounds, or not.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: On the map you haven't marked -- you didn't say he succumbed to his injuries on that spot, but you marked on the map the spot where he was, in fact, killed. I want you to tell the Trial Chamber how you were able to mark on that map that that was the spot where he was killed, as opposed to succumbed to his injuries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again we seem to be cross-examining, and the Defence has noted that the witness did not say whether he had been killed or not. The witness placed an "X" on the spot he, the Prosecutor, suggested that he should say where the killing took place. So this is the first time that the witness is actually telling us what he knows about Zvonko Rajic's death and making that clearer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now turn to the Prosecution. In the document marked P13, the witness indicated in which spot the man was killed. The mere fact that he indicated in which spot that he was present at the time, and he did say a while ago - I look at the transcript - he was 200 metres away from the spot where the body was, and he discovered that Rajic was there. He didn't know whether the man was alive or not. This is what he told us. So you can ask further questions, but he tells us under oath that he was not there at the time the man in question was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I -- I intent to move on from the area of Dusina at the moment. I may revisit it later at some point. I'll move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness BA, yesterday you gave some evidence to the Trial Chamber about the fact that your company was stationed in the Zenica Music School at the time of the attack on Dusina in January 1993. This isn't the question; this is just to introduce it to you. Your evidence was that at the time you were stationed in the Zenica Music School the basement was used as a storage facility. When your unit moved out of the Zenica Music School, who moved in or who took control of the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Was that the military police of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What was the 7th -- what were the military police using the Zenica Music School for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were using it as a place where the members of the military police were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What were they using the basement for -- for what -- I withdraw that. No, I don't. What were they using the basement for after they moved in and you moved out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a prison.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: A prison for who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For prisoners.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Civilians or prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about something that happened in April 1993 near Zmajevac. Can you tell the Trial Chamber about meeting some people in Zmajevac or near Zmajevac, which is in Zenica, in about April 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't refer to it as meeting.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Well, tell the Trial Chamber what happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the second conflict with the HVO - that means we were on Zmajevac Hill - and in a house, civilians were sort of captured: Two men, two women, and a child.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who captured them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our unit members.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you one of them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What did you do with these people you captured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my co-fighters, I was told to take them out of the zone where there was shooting.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where did you take them to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where is Tetovo in relation to Zenica? There's a -- there's a large map just behind you, if you wish to refer to that. It may assist. It's P1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part here.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Can you just describe it. It's just above Zenica on the map; is that correct? I'm sorry, I can't quite see from here. Can you just describe what's immediately below where you were pointing to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's downstream from Zenica, so downstream, down the River Bosna on the left-hand bank, near the Zenica iron works.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. And on the map you just pointed to, it's just north of Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: For the record, you're indicating -- or you indicated on the large map, P1, just below the words -- the large word "Zenica," in between Zenica and where it's written "smokestack."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, you said you were told to take the witnesses -- sorry, the civilians in that -- towards Tetovo, which is where you just showed us on the map. Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reached the crossroads, in the centre of Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What happened when you reached the crossroads? What did you meet -- who did you meet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And was that Serif Patkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And what did he tell you to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I should let the two women and child go and take the two men into the school --

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: -- take the two men --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak up. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Sorry. Witness BA, would you be able to speak up. I know you've got a soft voice, but the interpreters have to be able to hear you. We heard your answer to take them to -- into the school. Are you referring to the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Did you take the two men to the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What did you do with the two men when you got to the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I handed them over to the members of the military police at the entrance.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were these two people you handed over -- sorry, what was the ethnicity of these two men that you handed over to the military police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think one of them was a Croat and the other a Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were they HVO members, VRS members, or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Whereabouts physically, in relation to the entrance to the music school did you hand them over? I mean, was it inside the building, outside the building; where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance to the building.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What did the military police do when you handed these two prisoners over to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the military policemen started beating the two.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: How did he do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: How? How you beat people.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Well, what did he use to beat them with and where did he beat them on their bodies?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly on their backs. I don't remember him using any instrument.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: How old were these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One was I think 55 to 60 years old, and the other one was younger, perhaps 35.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What was your response to this military police officer beating the prisoners you handed over to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite simply I said to one of the policemen that he should stop beating the people. I can't explain. Probably I felt sorry for them. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
