utterances.text: You've just told us you visited the music school in April 1993 by taking two prisoners there. Now, what about in June 1993? Did you visit the music school and go inside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You've told us about the use of the basement as a detention centre during the war. Did you go to the basement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up to the entrance to the basement.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Could you describe the entrance to the basement to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You go down the stairs, and you come to a door.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What sort of door was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly what kind.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Why did you go there in June 1993? What had you heard about the music school that led you to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of curiosity.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What had fed your curiosity? What had you heard that made you curious to go to the basement where the prisoners were being kept?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were there any prisoners in the basement when you went to the basement door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: How many prisoners were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. I saw two or three from the entrance, but I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the prisoners you could see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't ask them.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you say whether they were POWs or civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What, if anything, had you heard about the ethnicity of the prisoners in detention there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What can you say about the reputation of the guards at the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what can you say? I don't know. I don't know in what sense you mean.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you whether you had heard anything about the reputation. Did they have a reputation for anything that you had heard of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's one thing what I heard and another what I saw. A moment ago I said I saw them beat two of the men there. I can't say they beat all of them when I didn't see it happen.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: No. But you've told the Trial Chamber that you went there in April 1993 and you handed over two prisoners who were beaten at the door. You then told us that you were curious and you went back there two months later and had a look in the basement yourself. My question is: What had you heard about the reputation of the guards or the place that led you back, in view of your experience of seeing prisoners being beaten at the door?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence counsel for Mr. Kubura is now taking the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Mr. Kubura considers that to be a leading question. The witness already answered it. Asked and answered. He said he hadn't heard anything about the reputation of the guards in the music school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He didn't say that, no. The transcript doesn't say that. It says, "What can you say? I don't know. I don't know in what sense you mean." I'm attempting to clarify it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may ask the question again -- or the Trial Chamber will ask the question. Have you heard on the part of -- or from people that were close to you, people from outside, any comments about the guards in the music school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard some comments, but the comments were not essential, so I don't see what purpose it would serve for me to say anything along those lines here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So he is telling us that he heard comments but these comments are irrelevant to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could we move into private session for a moment, please, Your Honours. It's an identity issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we shall now go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, are you able to say whether the guards had a reputation for anything, as opposed to the place having a reputation? And I mean by name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, because I didn't see it. I didn't see any one of them being harsher than the others.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What was the Zenica KP Dom used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: That mean correctional centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you aware of prisoners being transferred from the Zenica Music School to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the prisoners who were captured were transported to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I'm talking about prisoners being moved from the Zenica Music School to the KP Dom. Were you aware of prisoners being captured, taken to the Zenica Music School, and then being transferred to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that people were being held captive in the music school, but I didn't escort anybody from the music school to the KP Dom, so I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you aware of things that prisoners from the Zenica Music School were saying about the music school when they got to the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't have occasion to be at the KP Dom with them.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you that. I'm asking you whether you heard. Did you hear from anyone at the KP Dom or anyone else about what prisoners were saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask a question?

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Are you seeking clarification of my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The question I'm asking you is not whether you were at the KP Dom but whether you heard from other people what the prisoners who were transferred to the KP Dom were saying about the Zenica Music School.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I ask a question? I'm asking you again. With your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, you may ask your question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I say that I heard something and I don't know who I heard it from and I can't give you his name, then what use would that be to the Court? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you answer the question I'm asking you, and that is -- and it seems implicit from the question you just asked me that you had heard things. If that is the case, can you please tell Their Honours what you had heard about what the prisoners were saying when they went to the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have the floor, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: If I may raise an objection. Many of the questions that the Prosecution has been asking the witness are, strictly speaking, hearsay questions. It's not what the -- the witness himself has seen but what somebody else might have seen, which the witness might have then heard from that person. The jurisprudence before the Tribunal is that yes, hearsay evidence may be admitted if it is relevant and reliable. However, this last question is more than hearsay. It's in fact double hearsay. It's what prisoners might have said to other people who then might have said it to the witness. And in those circumstances, I would object to this evidence being given, as that it's so far removed from what might have happened. If there are witnesses who heard that themselves or saw it themselves, they could always be called by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, it goes directly to the question of notice. It may at the moment seem slightly prefer the peripheral. But as Your Honours are aware, the Prosecution case is of the accused having notice or inquiry notice of what was occurring at the Zenica Music School. Our case is that if this witness or other witnesses are able to say -- no, members of the brigade were able to say what was going on. That, in combination with documents and other elements that we intend to lead, at the end of the trial will be sufficient to prove either actual notice or inquiry notice. In relation to the question of the admissibility of otherwise of hearsay before the International Tribunal, I'm quoting from Archbold's "International Criminal Courts: Practice, Procedure and Evidence", the authors of whom are Mr. Dixon himself and Mr. Karim A. Khan, Barrister, and His Honour Judge May of Trial Chamber I: "There is no rule governing the admissibility of hear evidence before the ICC, ICTY, ICTR or Special Courts. The Trial Chambers of ICTY and ICTR have refrained from adopting a practice to exclude all hearsay evidence. There is in effect no rule declaring hearsay evidence per se inadmissible. The general scheme for the admissibility of evidence is set out in Rule 89 for both the ICTY and ICTR has guided the Chambers in their deliberations about hearsay evidence." The learned authors of this seminal text, the first text actually gathering the procedural laws in detail for the International Criminal Tribunals now in existence then go on to quote the Tadic Trial Chamber decision on the motion of hearsay from 1996 and the Aleksovski Appeals Chamber decision on the use that can be made of hearsay. I have copies of this if Your Honours wish to see an extract. It's in English. I can't produce a French version, a translation, at the moment. Finally, I'd point out to Your Honours that the Prosecution is obviously asking these particular questions of this witness for a reason; that is, a reason based upon a statement or a proofing session. And we wouldn't be going down this line if we didn't think we could make the evidence relevant, if not now, at a later point when Your Honours come to consider the evidence in its totality. So in the Prosecution's submission, the evidence - although at the moment it may seem a little tangential - will ultimately prove to be relevant and probative. Do Your Honours wish me to hand up copies from the extract of Archbold?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has noticed the comments made by the counsel of Mr. Kubura, as well as the answer provided by the Prosecution. Regarding this particular comment, it hinges on the fact that the witness through hearsay may have been informed about a number of things which would highlight the truth, thereby providing some information to the Trial Chamber. If I turn to the transcript, I realise that the question was put to him, and he was asked whether he was present or not in this detention centre, and he answered by saying that he had been there on one occasion and that as far as he knew he did not know who was inside. He was then asked a question about the relationship he may have had with someone in this centre. He said that he had had no information from this person. So to the various questions that were put to him, the witness may have been in contradiction with what he stated beforehand. He states today that he cannot provide any information thereof. This is where we stand now. I shall now ask him to tell us whether he has heard about the detention conditions of the prisoners. Can the witness answer this very simple question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So you heard about this. Have you heard about this in vague or concrete terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was nothing precise that was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those people who are mentioned, were these people actually working in this detention centre or are we talking about other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard it from a young guy working in the KP Dom Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The man who was working at the KP Dom in Zenica, did this man describe what he had seen with his own eyes? Did he describe things in very clear terms or in vague terms to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In vague terms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you feel that what he was telling you was particularly important or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if I understand you well, you can't tell the Judges anything about the detention conditions at the KP Dom in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't, because I was never up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have asked the witness a number of questions. He has answered by saying that he cannot contribute anything and that he cannot provide any information about these events that occurred at the KP Dom in Zenica, and that according to him a guard would have mentioned this but in very vague terms to him. Would the Prosecution wish to proceed? Would you like to change the topic and move on to another one?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just seek clarification. Maybe we're at cross-purposes. Your Honour just asked questions about the KP Dom in Zenica. I was actually asking about the Zenica Music School, about prisoners who had been transferred from the music school to the KP Dom and what the prisoners there had said about conditions in the Zenica Music School. The answer Your Honour seems to have elicited, according to the transcript, seems to relate to the KP Dom rather than to the music school. That was what I was trying to clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So if you wish to, clarify this issue by asking a question about the fate of those people that were at the music school and that were transferred to the KP Dom. But I think he has already answered the question, but I think he didn't know. But please ask him the question again, if you way.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, my question is just this: What did you hear that prisoners from the Zenica Music School who were transferred to the Zenica KP Dom were saying about what had happened to them at the Zenica Music School?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't say that anything was happening to them specifically, but it was just this worker in the KP Dom of Zenica that I heard that the prisoners coming from the music school would say they had poor conditions. Now, how far that was true or not, whether they exaggerated or not, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Poor conditions? Meaning what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I heard. Poor conditions were referred to. I can't say what those were. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. We'll move to another topic, and that is the ABiH -- or the combat between the ABiH and the HVO in the Ovnak, Susanj, Grahovcici, Brajkovici area in June 1993. Your company, did it participate on HVO manoeuvres in that area in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a map, which is a larger copy of P1, specifically in that area. What I want you to do is get the large black texter and please mark, in a moment, starting with where your company was and where it went to. Same thing; large line with arrows.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You're indicating on the map from the area of Rebrovac in the direction of Novo Selo. Does Novo Selo have another name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called it Ovnak.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Ovnak, O-v-n-a-k. You can see Ovnak is not marked on the map. Is Novo Selo another local name for what is also called Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. The arrow you have drawn goes just before Novo Selo. Could that also be described as the Susanj area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Susanj is on the right.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where did your unit go from the area you have marked on the map? That's the Novo Selo/Ovnak area. Did you go into the village of Susanj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on the question.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. I'll come to it -- I'll come back to it in a moment. You can see below on the map is Grahovcici. Did other units from the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade attack Grahovcici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly which unit attacked this place.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where were the civilians when your unit moved into Ovnak/Susanj area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, mostly there weren't any civilians there.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Was the HVO there then when you moved into the village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly there was withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You've mentioned before that Serif Patkovic was the commander. Was he there on that day leading the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who was leading the attack?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly the commanders of the platoons and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who was your commander on the day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: When you entered Susanj, how many members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, roughly, were in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit entered Novo Selo. It didn't go to Susanj. And in that combat position, you can't see all the units. Every unit is doing its own job. Now, who was there, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago mostly there weren't any civilians in Ovnak when you moved into it. Where were the civilians, or what did you see -- what civilians did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly the civilians -- or rather, that was the members of the HVO -- were in a mining area and were withdrawing towards Vitez from there.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Was UNPROFOR in the area; that is, the international peace-keeping troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you given any orders in relation to UNPROFOR, to do anything in relation to UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What were the orders and who gave them to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received orders to go down to a place that was lower towards Zenica, not to allow anybody to pass through that way.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I just asked you about UNPROFOR, and you said not to allow anybody to pass through that way. Does your answer mean not to allow UNPROFOR to pass through that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not UNPROFOR or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Was it Serif Patkovic who gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to me personally, no.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who did he give the order to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: How do you know he gave the order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you have the floor, the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered the question. The question was a leading one. He didn't say that Patkovic issued the order, which the Prosecution suggested, but the witness did provide an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not hear the translation. I'm sorry. Could you repeat, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to react to the question posed by the Prosecutor because the witness -- he suggested to the witness that he had said something earlier on which he didn't in fact say. But there's no need for me to object and react because the witness himself stated this clearly. He said he did not know that Patkovic ever issued the order.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, where do you go on that day when you were ordered to stop anyone entering the village? What other places did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Cajdras.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What about the next day? Where did you go then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next day I was in Novo Selo.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were other members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Novo Selo the next day, that is, Ovnak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I would just like to clarify something. I have just read the transcript and the question raised by the Prosecution; to that question, the witness answered that he had been ordered and that the UNPROFOR had told them that nobody should be able to go that way and that they should bar the route. And when another question was put to him, the Prosecution said or insinuated that he had been given the order that nobody should enter the village, which is not what the witness said. I would just like to clarify this and make sure that it's put on the record correctly. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber did see that, pertaining to the question which was asked, the question relating to UNPROFOR. The witness answered, without us being able to understand whether his answer related to UNPROFOR forces or some other event. Therefore, we cannot draw the conclusion that his answer was directly connected with the presence of UNPROFOR. So we need to clarify this point, I believe -- if this question is relevant, of course, and the Trial Chamber does wonder whether it is relevant or not. So I shall give the floor to the Prosecution. If the Prosecution wishes to ask that question again on the presence of UNPROFOR forces in that area and how the group of the witness and UNPROFOR operated or not.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was saying that the Trial Chamber has noted the Defence's position. The Defence wishes to see this point clarified. You can ask your question again, but I would like to say that we shall be stopping in ten minutes to have our break.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wasn't seeking clarification, in light of the answer the witness gave in relation to Serif Patkovic. I wasn't going to take it any further.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, a moment ago I got to the point where --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Excuse me. I've just got to find the transcript again.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The question was: The next day, were other members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in Novo Selo or Ovnak? And you answered yes. What were they doing the next day in Ovnak, or Novo Selo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mostly deployed there, because you can't fight in one place and then withdraw the very next day.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The civilians had gone and the soldiers were there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What were the soldiers doing in relation to the civilians' houses and their property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the belongings from the houses were collected together in one spot.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What sort of belongings? Describe them, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly household appliances, technical goods.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You said were collected together in one spot. Who collected them and put them in that spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Is that soldiers of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Soldiers of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What about other brigades?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And what was the spot where they were collected together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The church at Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you one of the people collecting these goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Did you go into the church in Brajkovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What did you see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of the thing things that had been collected there.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You just described mostly household appliances. What other things, other than household appliances, did you see in the church? And approximately how full was the church of these things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was quite a lot of them. There were quite a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. The other part of the question was: What else besides household appliances did you see there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly technical goods.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You mentioned household goods and appliances and technical goods. What about vehicles, motor vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where were they and how many were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly they were used for the requirements of the army. I don't know how many.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And where were they parked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, two or three in front of the church and others had been driven off by the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And how long did your unit remain in Novo Selo/Ovnak area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps three days, three or four days. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who was in charge of gathering all these -- all the civilian property that was in the church?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. What do you mean by "in charge," "who was in charge"?

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Who was guarding the church, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole settlement was being guarded, Ovnak, Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where did the contents of the church, that is, the civilian property, go from there? I mean, what happened to it all? Who received it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of it went to the brigade. Whether everything went, I don't know; and who got the goods ultimately, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Part of it went to the brigade. The brigade, was it then stationed at Bilmiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Are you saying part of the property that was in the church in Brajkovici was taken back to brigade headquarters in Bilmiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Where was it stored -- or where was it taken to in brigade headquarters in Bilmiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, in some premises that were designated as a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's 5.30, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is now 5.30. We shall resume at five minutes to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated] Before I give the floor to the Prosecution, I would like to know whether in the time that we have left you will be able to finish your line of questioning, or would you wish to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm very hopeful we should be able to continue -- finish tonight, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So I give you the floor. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, before the break, you were telling the Trial Chamber about the storing of the civilian property from Ovnak/Susanj area in brigade headquarters in Bilmiste. Yesterday you told the Trial Chamber that the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade headquarters were in an educational facility or a school in Bilmiste. What I want you to do is to draw a diagram for the Trial Chamber of the facility in Bilmiste, please. If you'd just -- I think you said that there were three buildings. Can you please draw the three buildings, a cross-sectional view, if you can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You've drawn three buildings. Can you please put numbers on them, 1, 2 -- sorry. First of all, how many floors did each of these buildings have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think three each.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you please just draw lines on the buildings to indicate the floors, which I think means putting two lines on each building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The building on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat his answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your last answer. The interpreters didn't hear it. So please, again, Witness BA, could you please speak up as loudly as you comfortably can.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the sports hall.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Where was the -- well, what I want you to do is to put a "1," "2," and " 3" on each -- above each of these buildings, please, starting from the left.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: 1 was the sports hall. Can you please write "sports hall" next to "1."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The building which you have marked number 2 has three floors; building number 3 also has three floors. What was the commander's office? Can you please mark that with a -- an "X."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You've marked it on the second building. Could you please draw an arrow from that leading to above the "2" and write in "commander's office," please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Now, with a circle, can you please mark the places where the goods from Ovnak/Susanj area were stored.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. And can you just on the diagram, say in the bottom left-hand corner, put in the "O" and put an "=" and just write in where goods were stored.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Could you please put in an "=" between the "O" and the "M."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You also mentioned earlier some cars. Were cars taken back to the brigade headquarters as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Are you able to mark on that particular diagram where the cars were taken to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you please just write under those six squares you have drawn "cars."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you also -- don't write but just point on that diagram to where the entrance to the brigade headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Are you indicating that it was around the corner in the part we can't see on building number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Can you just draw a curved arrow to where you say the entrance was and just write next to it "brigade headquarters entrance."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And what's the approximate distance between those parked cars you've indicated there on the map and the brigade headquarters entrance in metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 20, 25 metres perhaps.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Would you just be able to draw a line with an arrow on each end and write "20m" for 20 metres on the arrow. You know, the way to indicate the distance between two points. That is, between the parked cars and the entrance door.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So that this can remain public, would it be if okay if the witness could write "BA" on the map, Your Honours. The Prosecution doesn't consider that would identify him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the initials "BA"? Could you initial this drawing, please, below the drawing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And please also mark the date on, which is the 9th of December, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What were the top two floors of building 3 used for, Witness BA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the accommodation of the 2nd and 3rd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Could you please do an arrow to each of the two floors and write in "accommodation 2nd Battalion and 3rd Battalion." If you could just do that on the right of building 3.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Could you please write in -- you've written "II and III Battalion." Could you just write in something to indicate that's where they were accommodated. And by "accommodated," do you mean as in billeted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Could you write something in to indicate that's where the soldiers were billeted, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What was the top floor of the second building used for, Witness BA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, the interpreters didn't catch your last answer. My question was: What was the top floor of the second building used for? Can you just repeat your answer, please, loudly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we can't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: They can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units attached to the staff.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You mean the corps -- sorry, the brigade command staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I mean.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The logistics platoon, the cooks, part of the artillery, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. Can you just please indicate on that map as well, just draw an arrow going out and up, and just put in who was housed there.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And what was building number 1, the sports hall, used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For sports activities, and sometimes it was used for some celebrations.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May that diagram be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Usher, could you show this document to the Defence team, as well as to the accused, please. Madam Registrar, could you give us a number, an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P14.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May the diagram that the witness marked of the area of Novo Selo, Ovnak, Susanj also be tendered into evidence. Do Your Honours wish the witness to mark that so it doesn't get lost along the way, if he puts his initials and the date on it, in case other witnesses at some point mark a similar document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to initial this document, to sign by using the initials "BA" and to write the date in, please.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, could you perhaps use the larger black marking pen rather than the smaller one. It's a black-and-white copy. And just make it a little bit larger than the last one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Could you show this document to the Defence again, the document that has just been initialled. Madam Registrar, could you give us an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The exhibit number is P15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exhibit is therefore P15. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, I'm going to show you some photographs now that will be shown on the screen in front of you. I'm going to show you four photographs. I'm going to ask you to identify, if you can, each of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then I'll ask them to be moved into evidence. And copies are actually on their way.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I'm showing you photo 0124-9067. Witness BA, what is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of Novo Selo and I think Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And could you just tell the Trial Chamber for the record where your unit was when it came -- from which direction your unit came into Novo Selo in June 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the left-hand side, to the left of the road.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And can you just describe to the Trial Chamber where your unit went to in Novo Selo on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from this side here, and it was there in Novo Selo. Afterwards, I was transferred to the checkpoint here at Ovnak, and I spent three or four days there.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, we can't see what you're pointing at. Can you just describe where in the photograph you were pointing to by some identifying feature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit came, as I said, from the direction, from the left here, the left area of the road.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: You're indicating at the very bottom of the photograph towards the road, which is running on the left side. Where did you move to then?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise. My case manager was actually moving it. I thought by some magic you were able to.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Can you just describe the area in the middle in which you actually -- the area you actually went to. Just describe it for the court record as you look at the photograph. Where was it? Top, bottom, middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see it on the photograph, the place I went to. It's not shown.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the next photograph, which is 0124-9070. That's the ERN.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What's this a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the peak of Ovnak and Novo Selo, the top.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: The third photo is 0124-9079. What is -- what does that depict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find my way around on this photograph, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: All right. We'll move to the next one, which is 67 -- sorry, 01396760, ERN 01248907. In your evidence before, you mentioned a church in Brajkovici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Do you recognise the church in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, I regret to say the copies of these photographs haven't arrived in -- we were trying to get colour copies. They haven't arrived in time. We had ordered them. So could these just be virtually marked, so to speak, the four numbers I've read onto the record. And we will tender, assuming there's no objection, the four photos when they actually get here, either later this afternoon or tomorrow. It shouldn't make any difference, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I find it difficult to give a virtual number here, on the basis of photographs which are virtual photographs, because we can only see them on a screen. Tomorrow morning you can tender these photographs into evidence. We'll leave this on standby for the moment, and we shall tender these photographs into evidence tomorrow, unless the Defence feels that these can already be tendered here and now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Except, of course, the third one, which the witness couldn't identify. I don't tender that. It's 1, 2, and 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence just had a remark to make with respect to the photograph that wasn't recognised by the witness. But as the Prosecutor has already said he's not tendering that one into evidence, thank you. That would be what I had to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So you will provide these three photographs tomorrow, the beginning of the afternoon, and we shall then give an exhibit number. That said, only three out of the four photographs will be tendered into evidence. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I want to take you, Witness BA, to combat operations between the HVO and the ABiH in the municipality and town of Vares in November 1993. I don't understand there to be any dispute between the party that is there was in fact -- there were in fact combat operations at that time, although we have not yet reached agreement on these latter actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No movement from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, did you participate in combat operations in Vares against the -- sorry, against the HVO in November 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Was your unit present in Vares in November, early November 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't a member of the 7th Muslim at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Were you in Vares in early November 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Mr. Witness BA, what can you tell the Trial Chamber about what happened in Vares in November 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Kubura's Defence team has an objection to make. The witness has already said he wasn't a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade during that period of time and that he wasn't in the region of Vares at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Before I give the floor back to you, can the witness tell us at what date exactly he left the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade? Because it seems like in November he was no longer a member of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the witness answers that, can I remind Your Honours of the witness's evidence yesterday morning -- yesterday about him being in the brigade 1993, 1994, and 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Can the witness tell us at what time he -- at what moment he left this brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday I just mentioned 1992 and 1993, when I first testified. I don't remember of what date exactly at the end of 1993 I ceased to be a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And why did the witness cease to be a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade? Did he leave voluntarily or was he asked to leave? What happened exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I was unemployed at the time, I managed to find a job, and that's why I left the brigade, to take up this new job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us exactly when this occurred. Was it in July, August, November? What months exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was soon after the operation at Ovnak. Perhaps a month later, at the most, when I left the brigade. I can't be sure of the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I give the floor back to the Prosecution. The witness has just told us that he left the 7th Brigade because he had found a job and that, therefore, in the month of November he was not in Vares. And if he had said yesterday -- or said yesterday that he was a member in 1992, 1993, and 1994, he qualifies this and says that he was a member in 1992 and 1993. In any event, he was no longer a member in the month of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just apologise. I wrongly intervened. I've just re-checked the transcript. I shouldn't have been so hasty. I should have just asked Your Honours to hold off for a moment while I checked the transcript. It didn't say 1994 and 1995 and I apologise for my incorrect intervention. It was something that was in my mind.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, I have another question. If you could just wait a moment. Witness BA, you've told the transcript about property from those villages -- of Susanj, Ovnak, and so on -- being taken back to brigade headquarters and stored in the spot you've indicated on the diagram, which is now P14. What happened to that property when it got back to brigade headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, some of the property was divided up among the members of the 7th Muslim Brigade. What exactly and how this was done, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Did you receive any property?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I left the brigade right after that.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Witness BA, you said that it was divided among the members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. As you know, the brigade was composed of officers, ordinary soldiers, commanders and so on. Was it divided -- how was it divided amongst the various components in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: We spoke yesterday, and you gave some evidence about the Mujahedin having a training camp at Arnauti. What do you know about the Mujahedin having houses in the Central Bosnian area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I know is that they didn't stay in the brigade. So if they came to the brigade, they spent a day or two there and then left.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: I'm asking you specifically about houses, Witness BA. What do you know about houses in which the Mujahedin stayed in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yesterday the witness testified that he knew about the camp at Arnauti, in which he underwent training. As to other questions pertaining to Central Bosnia, he said he had no personal knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber has noted your comment. Please proceed. The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Are you able to answer the question, Witness BA, that is, about houses in which the Mujahedin were staying in Central Bosnia? Do you have any knowledge of it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew about one house which they purchased and where they lived.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: And where was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Zenica.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that the emir of the brigade was called Emir Karalic. And you also spoke about a break between the Mujahedin and the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Were you aware of any dispute between the Mujahedin and Emir Karalic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about a dispute, a quarrel, which I was not present at.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What did you hear the dispute was about between Emir Karalic and the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that there were several hodza in the brigade. Can you tell us their names.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the names you want?

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember their names.

utterances.speaker: THE OFFICE OF THE
utterances.text: What do you know about the Mujahedin -- El Mujahedin unit or detachment within the ABiH 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already said that he left the 7th Muslim Brigade at the end of June. And the second point: Yesterday, in response to your question, he said loud and clear - and you repeated it - that he didn't know much about the structure of the corps and brigades. And third, the witness is being suggested that the Mujahedin was within the frameworks of the 3rd Corps, although that particular fact has not been mentioned or confirmed by anyone thus far. So for those three reasons I consider that these questions do not merit an answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the Defence comment is concerned, what does -- what is the Prosecution's position, in the light of the fact that the witness provided no information yesterday on the -- on the integration of the 7th Muslim Brigade to the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just asking based upon some thing which is are in his statement and which the witness has told me and other prosecutors in proofing and is not necessarily related to anything my learned friend, Mrs. Residovic, is saying at the moment. There is a purpose for me asking this question based upon his statement, irrespective of whether he could tell us about the formal structure of the 3rd Corps yesterday. The two are completely unrelated. I'm asking him what is his knowledge of the El Mujahed detachment. He may have a different date to that the Defence has in mind. As there's no agreement, it appears, on the date of formation, I should be able to ask this witness was what he knows about the formation, as he was a member of the brigade at a possibly pertinent point during 1993. It's relative and probative, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. At this stage of the proceeding, the witness can answer this question which was put to him concerning this particular unit; did he know about it or did he not. I shall ask him the question directly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, when you were a member of the 7th Brigade, did you know is that another unit called El Mujahedin unit existed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that unit never existed, while I myself was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This unit, therefore, did not exist at the time you were a member of the 7th Brigade. That, in effect, is what you are telling us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yesterday you told us that at one stage you had been trained at Arnauti, at a training camp, together with a number of other people who, according to you, were strangers. Which unit did these people belong to? Or were you talking about civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which unit they belonged to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How much time did you spend at this training camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, about 20 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was this a military training camp or were you being taught how to cook? Could you tell us a little bit, whether you were being taught to shoot, close combat -- were you being taught close combat operations? What were you being taught? Or were you being taught how to sew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. And you spent 20 days with your fellow trainees. You did not talk to them. You did not exchange views or opinions with these people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore you had no contact whatsoever with these people.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the contact I had was through the training sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you didn't ask them where they came from, what they were doing there, and why they were there, basically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where they came from exactly. I think the initial -- during the initial training, I think they were from Turkey. Mostly the military training was the kind that we needed, so nobody asked many questions. Nobody asked anybody anything, in actual fact. So the object of the training was to learn something about weapons, to get some preparatory training and preparation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How many of you were there, then? Were you 10, 20, or 30? How many trainees were there in this camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps 20, 25, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And out of these 25, how many were locals of the region, compared with other people who did not come from that region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were about 20 or 25 of us. I don't remember; perhaps 3 or 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness tells us that he doesn't know anything about this unit, and the three or four people that were with him are people he was literally not in contact with. Please proceed your line of questions. We have 20 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's some clarification. I wasn't actually asking him about the training in 1992 in Arnauti, whatever it's called - I can't remember - I was asking him about the formation of a detachment called El Mujahed sometime in 1993. The two are unrelated.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Witness BA, I want to ask you about the accused Amir Kubura over there. Was the accused Amir Kubura based at the educational facility in Bilmiste when you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did you ever see the accused Amir Kubura at Bilmiste, Witness BA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once or twice.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: What was his position when you were there in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: When you were at Bilmiste in 1993, what was Amir Kubura's position within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to what position, Amir Kubura knows more about that -- or rather, I know from the press or from the -- this trial. I didn't notice the man at all at the time. I just saw him once or twice. I don't know, as I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Who was the commanding officer of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in 1993? You must know that, Witness BA.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: In 1993, who was the commanding officer of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, in our brigade, as far as I remember, and as far as I know, it was said that Mr. Amir Kubura was abroad. Now, whether that was the right information, I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about President Izetbegovic. Did he have any relationship with the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Defence has the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence counsel of Mr. Kubura would like to object. It is quite obvious that Witness BA was an ordinary soldier, and he knows nothing about the relationship of Mr. Izetbegovic and the command staff, commanding officers, and his relationship with the 7th Muslim Brigade. He cannot know that as an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, how can he not know that as an ordinary soldier? He was there. With great respect to my learned friend, I'm asking him what his knowledge was. Either he knows or he doesn't know. And if he does know, he might be able to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as this issue is concerned, I feel we can ask this question to a soldier, a man in the army, ask him whether the acting president in the state in which he lives is someone whom he knows and whether this president - in this particular case, Mr. Izetbegovic - whether he ever saw him. And the question is a very banal one. This does not prejudice anybody in any way. We are just asking the witness whether the name Izetbegovic is a name which he has heard and whether he ever met the president.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question actually, Your Honour, is: Are you aware of any relationship between the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and President Izetbegovic? And again, I'm asking it, as the Defence knows, based on the witness's statement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I know is that President Izetbegovic visited on several occasions the 7th Muslim Brigade, just as he visited the corps. He would tour all the units. Now, if you can extract something from that kind of relationship, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: I want to ask you about discipline within the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. And obviously I'm only asking you as an ordinary soldier what you knew about discipline within the brigade, to head off any possible objections to this line of questioning. The 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, you've told us, had military police. What did the military police do and were they used to enforce discipline and how did they do so? Can you please give me an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Discipline in the 7th Muslim Brigade was set at the start. When you came to the 7th Muslim, there was no mistreatment of any kind. You just lived that way, according to Muslim customs, and the conduct of each and every member of the Muslim Brigade was linked to that.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were you aware of any soldiers, apart from the instances you described yesterday of soldiers being detained at the correctional facility for theft and also for alcohol, drinking alcohol, were you aware of any soldiers in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade being prosecuted for criminal offences such as those against the Geneva Conventions and the Laws of War you told us that you were told about yesterday, in your time at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS BA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That completes the examination-in-chief. Your Honours, I have an application I wish to make in the absence of the witness in relation to his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. I must tell the witness that he needs to come back tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. I would kindly ask him to be here at 2.00, an tomorrow the Defence counsels of the two accused will ask him questions. Can the Defence team tell us approximately how much time they will need tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the cross-examination by General Hadzihasanovic's Defence will not be lengthy, but I just have to consult today's testimony, the transcript of it, and I assume that it might take half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you very much. Mr. Kubura's counsel now, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, about the same time for the Kubura Defence team.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. So we'll need an hour. And the Prosecution may wish to re-examine the witness. The Trial Chamber may also wish to ask the witness a number of questions. So, Witness, you shall now be leaving the courtroom and you shall be returning here at 2.00, 2.00 p.m. And I believe that at around 4.00 you will be able to return home and the flight has been organised for you. So see you again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution has -- I have an application which we reluctantly make, and I'm sure Your Honours have some inkling of what I'm about to say. Your Honours, the Prosecution -- the Prosecution provided Your Honours with a copy of the witness's statement some weeks ago for Your Honours' pre-trial-preparation purposes. Your Honours this morning reminded the witness of his rights under Rule 89(E) in relation to self-incrimination. The witness's testimony in some significant regards has been at odds with the -- with both the statement the witness provided to the Prosecution, which was signed last year, and in two proofing sessions we had on Sunday and Monday. The Prosecution confirmed with the witness on both Sunday and Monday that the information contained in his statement was in fact correct. The Prosecution, pursuant to Your Honours' ruling last week, provided the witness with a copy of his statement to take home and make any changes that he felt were necessary in B/C/S -- in his own language -- to the statement. The witness the next day came back and had a proofing session, which he made several minor corrections to the statement. He didn't write on the statement, but he marked on the edges of the statement those bits of the statement which he considered to be slightly incorrect. One, for example, was a translation of "Blue Falcons," which was translated as "blue hawks" into Bosnian, which is why it was in fact corrected. I attempted to lead evidence from the witness in accordance with his statement, given to the Prosecution, and what he had told me and an investigator and two different translators on Sunday and Monday of this week which, as far as the Prosecution was concerned up until at least midday, when we bid him farewell yesterday, was in fact a correct version of the evidence he was going to give. The witness has departed from his evidence -- from his statement and the instructions he gave the Prosecution yesterday in several significant, very significant features. Your Honours will of course appreciate from the summary the most significant is the witness told the Prosecution yesterday and in fact signed a statement to the effect that he had directly witnessed the death of Zvonko Rajic and that Serif Patkovic, the commanding officer of the 2nd Battalion, his commanding officer, had in fact shot Zvonko Rajic. The witness has made a number of other, in evidence -- has also substantially changed other parts of his evidence. There are quite a few, and I don't have the time at the moment to go right through them. The application is this, Your Honour: The Prosecution seeks the Trial Chamber's leave to cross-examine the witness in relation to inconsistencies between the statement he provided and the evidence he has given. The Prosecution isn't in a position tonight to outline each and every one of those inconsistencies, because we have to go back and look at the transcript and compare it to the relevant portions of his statement and his evidence. The Prosecution very reluctantly makes this application because we were hoping that the witness would give evidence that was truthful in all respects, and of course the Prosecution is very mindful of the way Your Honours have approached it and the fact that the witness has given evidence on his oath about various things. However, there is a precedent -- there are several precedents in the Tribunal for allowing the Prosecution to treat a witness as adverse or hostile to the common-law method of dealing with the witness of a party, and I can refer Your Honours directly to two Trial Chamber rulings; one of Trial Chamber I and one of Trial Chamber II. The first one is in the Brdjanin and Talic trial, a ruling of His Honour Judge Agius on the 23rd of January, 2002 at page 677 of the transcript, where the Trial Chamber ruled on the application of the Prosecution that the -- a party producing a witness could ask the permission of the Trial Chamber to treat that witness as adverse or hostile - I'm just paraphrasing - and you would be able to put to him prior out-of-court statements and cross-examine him as to what he said before and what he said in court and to try and elicit the truthful version, which one is true. The second one was in relation to a motion the Prosecution filed in October this year. That was on the 20th of October this -- sorry, the 16th of October in the case of Blagojevic and Jokic. That was Trial Chamber I. And the motion is headed "Prosecution's motion for leave to ask leading questions of adverse witnesses if necessary." His Honour Judge Liu ruled on the motion on the 20th of October 2003, granting the Prosecution motion. In granting the Prosecution motion, the -- His Honour Judge Liu said - and this is at page 3102 and 3103 of the transcript - "As a practice all proceedings should be conducted in accordance with the normal way, that is, try to avoid the leading questions by examination-in-chief. But anyway, if the Prosecution finds that there is any inconsistency with the previous statement of the witness -- or sorry, or the witness tries to avoid the -- to answer the questions, the Prosecution should refer to matter to the Chamber and the Chamber will decide whether to allow this witness to answer that question. And at some occasions we might go to the private sessions to hear the answer of that witness. By saying so, the motion of the Prosecution is granted." I note the time, Your Honours. It's one minute to 7.00. This is a fairly important issue in respect of this witness's evidence and the summary we provided. Could I ask Your Honours to allow me to complete addressing you on this point tomorrow morning, or if the legal officer from Chambers would like you to provide us with anything in writing or any decisions -- any other decisions we can find. We haven't been able to find anything from the Appeals Chamber, but we have looked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The question you are raising before the Trial Chamber is to understand whether the Trial Chamber can authorise you to question the witness, given the fact that the witness has made statements which are contrary to what he has said before. This is an important case, and these questions can only be put if you file a request in writing so that the Defence team can state its position. We shall render a decision pursuant to the request, and in the event that you request the witness again. In that case, the witness has to be brought back again. But I would like to remind you Rule 39 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence means that the Prosecutor can question witnesses, but this Rule stipulates that there is a clear distinction between the witnesses, the victims, and the suspects. Now, as far as the suspects are concerned, when this examination is being conducted you should stipulate to the witness that he or she has a number of rights so that the person has the right to remain silent, has the right to be defended by a counsel, and when the suspect wishes to remain silent, then the procedure is quite special. Here, as regards Witness BA, we face a particular situation. This witness is not suspect. He's being examined and questioned as a simple witness. He makes statements which are made in -- as the procedure unfolds, which are less stringent than those mentioned in Article 49. It so happens that his answers do not tally with what he has said previously. So as you know, these are oral proceedings; what counts is what the witnesses actually tell us when they are being called and when they answer the questions put to them by the Prosecution and when they answer the questions put to them by the Defence teams. According to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, nothing seems to prevent a simple witness, an ordinary witness, to make a statement in a given period of time and to adopt a different position at a different time. What counts is what he tells us under oath. Let me remind you that pursuant to Rule 39 he does not make the solemn declaration -- he is not made to make a solemn declaration. The conditions of this questioning is something which is out of the control of the Trial Chamber, and the potential rights of the witness is not something that he is aware of, even though he were in the position to be a suspect witness, he may turn around and say, "I have nothing to say." And you raise, therefore, an important question which deserves a request in writing and a response by the Defence. On two occasions you say that this Tribunal was -- ruled on these two points, and we can only answer your question in writing. If we feel that the witness can be questioned again, then we'll have ample time to bring -- to call the witness back again. As things stand today, we ask you to file a request in writing in which you are asked to spell out the most important points and then we will proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just one more minute. Since the Prosecutor has said that he has completed the examination-in-chief of the witness, I should like to ask the Trial Chamber to confirm that we start the cross-examination of this witness tomorrow, and after that we shall decide on the proposals made by the Prosecution. Have I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
