utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kubura's Defence team, anything to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is the identical position of the Kubura Defence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was in error. I apologise. I was in error when I said I completed my examination-in-chief. Whey meant to say was subject to Your Honours' ruling on that point. The Prosecution does not consider its examination-in-chief finished until that important point is resolved. And as Your Honour quite rightly says, it's something on we should file written submissions and it should be responded to. So could I propose a practical solution, and that the Prosecution be allowed not to close its case with that witness for the moment, because, as I've said, it's a very important issue and there are other Trial Chamber decisions on this point. We have other witnesses here at the moment waiting to give evidence. They've been brought here at Tribunal expense. Could Witness BA be allowed to return home and -- Your Honours, we will file something fairly soon in relation to that. We obviously have to go through the evidence and the statements and compare the two and put proper reasons in writing -- allow him to go home and allow the Prosecution to call the other two witnesses tomorrow? The reason I say this is because it may impact upon the cross-examination of the Defence. If we call other evidence in relation to the matters I outlined, it may have some impact on the way the Defence cross-examines Witness BA. So my -- the Prosecution proposes that we adjourn BA's evidence and continue with other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You raise another question. You ask us to interrupt the examination-in-chief so that we can answer your question in writing, which makes the witness situation rather difficult. He would then need to go home, could -- might find it difficult in such a situation, whereas he is here now. Also, the Trial Chamber, if seized with this matter, early tomorrow morning can render a decision in writing. But the difficulty arises because the Defence must respond in writing and the Defence will undoubtedly not be ready. Given that you have all night to prepare your submission in writing, tomorrow morning we can be seized with this matter, but the Defence team will not be able to respond because the hearing resumes tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. So if you feel that the examination-in-chief is completed and that the Defence team can proceed with its cross-examination, I think it would be better that you call the witness back afterwards. But as things stand today, we cannot ask the witness to go home now and you will come back in a few months' time because, as regards their testimony, I think we will not be quite sure about the way in which this testimony was conducted. He is testifying today and is not under any pressure whatsoever. This is what I suggest, which I think is the wisest solution, which is very much in line with the Rules of this Tribunal: I think we should proceed with the cross-examination tomorrow. You can ask him further questions tomorrow. And Prosecution, you can re-examine the witness if you so wish. And in that case, you can file your submission and the witness can be re-examined at a later stage. We find ourself in the situation where a witness is not suspect; he has made a number of statements that have been taken in which he was not -- it was not made known to him that he had any kind of rights. He was not asked to make these statements under oath. And today the witness is taking up a position which is not in line with what the Prosecution expected. So as you know, we have different -- witnesses come and go. And what is important to us and what he says under oath. He has said a number of things today under oath. So therefore, we shall resume tomorrow at quarter past 2.00. You can, of course, file your written submission and inform the Defence about this and tell them what this submission contains so that they -- the Defence can respond. The court stands adjourned. We shall resume tomorrow at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be resumed on Wednesday, the 10th day of December, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.

--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.10 p.m.,
